newsitem.title: JAPAN: S&P says credit quality of Japan carriers weaker.
newsitem.headline: S&P says credit quality of Japan carriers weaker.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Corp said on Thursday that the credit quality of the Japanese airline industry has weakened amid ongoing deregulation and major changes in market conditions.
Airlines have offered limited or delayed responses to these challenges because of their faith in "cooperative competition" and their historically strong business fundamentals, the rating agency said.

Japan Airlines Co Ltd (JAL) needs to bolster its profitability ahead of further deregulation and capacity increases, and failure to do so could lead to a downgrade, it said. JAL is currently rated BBB+, it added.

All Nippon Airways Co Ltd (ANA) is rated BBBpi, reflecting a slightly better market position among its domestic peers, S&P said. But ANA's business risk has increased over the past decade due to aggressive expansion into the competitive international market, it said.
Japan Air System Co Ltd is rated BBpi, reflecting its reliance on unprofitable local domestic routes and a weak financial profile, it said.
However, although Japanese airlines face major changes in the business environment, they still benefit from being based in one of the world's largest and steadily growing markets, it said.
